plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 14: Fluid Mechanics
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a shaded perspective drawing of a clear cylindrical container partly filled with a pale blue liquid. The vessel has an elliptical rim with a thick rounded glass lip, a slightly darker band marking the liquid surface a short way down, and a darker pooled region across the curved bottom. Three small cubes outlined in black dashed lines sit at different places within the liquid, each drawn in the container's perspective and each carrying a numeral: cube 1 high and toward the left, cube 2 a little lower and to the right, and cube 3 near the bottom center. A curved arrow links each cube to its own label, written as a ratio in tall parentheses with a subscript, reading Δm/ΔV with subscript 1 at the upper right, Δm/ΔV with subscript 2 at the middle right, and Δm/ΔV with subscript 3 out to the left. Giving each sampling cube its own subscripted mass-to-volume ratio invites the reader to treat the three as separate numbers rather than one value for the whole vessel, which is how local density is defined point by point.

elements: Transparent cylindrical glass container (open top), thin pale blue-green wall
Thick rounded glass rim/lip drawn as a torus-like elliptical ring at the top
Inner elliptical opening of the rim
Pale blue liquid column filling the lower ~2/3 of the cylinder
Slightly darker elliptical band marking the liquid free surface a short way down from the rim
Darker pooled/shaded region across the curved inner bottom of the container
Dashed-outline sample cube 1, upper-left region inside the liquid, labelled '1'
Dashed-outline sample cube 2, mid-right region inside the liquid, labelled '2'
Dashed-outline sample cube 3, near bottom center inside the liquid, labelled '3'
Curved arrow from label 1 (upper right, outside vessel) pointing left-down to cube 1
Curved arrow from label 2 (middle right, outside vessel) pointing left to cube 2
Curved arrow from label 3 (left, outside vessel) pointing right to cube 3
Label text (Δm/ΔV)₁ in tall parentheses at upper right
Label text (Δm/ΔV)₂ in tall parentheses at middle right
Label text (Δm/ΔV)₃ in tall parentheses at left
Numeric readout of Δm, ΔV and their ratio for the currently selected cube

interactions.teaches: Density is evaluated at a chosen point: clicking cube 1, 2 or 3 highlights that dashed volume and shows its own Δm/ΔV, so the three are separate local numbers rather than one value for the whole vessel.

interactions.label: Sample cube edge (relative)
interactions.teaches: Shrinking the sampling cube makes Δm and ΔV both shrink, but their ratio settles on a fixed value — local density is the limit of Δm/ΔV as the surrounding volume becomes small.

interactions.label: Fluid model
interactions.teaches: In a uniform liquid all three ratios are equal (one bulk density); in a heterogeneous liquid the deeper cubes read larger ratios, so density becomes a function of position.
The three sample cubes sit at different depths and different distances into the vessel, not on a flat plane — rotating reveals their true 3D placement inside the liquid column.

demo_steps.title: One bulk density
demo_steps.narration: In a uniform liquid, each dashed cube returns the same Δm/ΔV. One number describes the whole vessel.

demo_steps.title: Sample cube 3 near the bottom
demo_steps.narration: Switch the fluid to heterogeneous: the deepest cube now measures a larger mass in the same volume, so (Δm/ΔV)₃ exceeds the others.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the sampling volume
demo_steps.narration: Drag the cube edge down. Δm and ΔV both collapse toward zero, yet their ratio stabilises — this limiting value is the local density at that point.

demo_steps.title: Compare all three points
demo_steps.narration: Back at full size, the three subscripted ratios are distinct numbers tied to three positions: density is defined point by point, not for the container as a whole.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cylinder: radius 1.2, wall height 3.0, centered on origin with base at y = -1.5 and rim at y = +1.5. Rim lip: torus of tube radius 0.10 at y = +1.5, radius 1.22, pale opaque blue-white #e8f2f5; inner opening ellipse visible through it. Liquid: solid cylinder radius 1.15 from y = -1.48 up to a free surface at y = +0.75 (about one quarter of the height below the rim). Free-surface disc slightly darker #b6cbe6 with a thin darker rim band; bottom pooled region a darker ellipse #9dbcdc across y = -1.45. Glass wall transparent #dff0f2 at ~0.15 opacity with a faint lighter vertical highlight on the left; liquid body #c5d8ee at ~0.55 opacity. Sample cubes: wireframe boxes with black dashed edges (#1a1a1a), default edge length 0.42 (slider scales 0.1–1.0 of a 0.85 max edge). Cube 1 at (-0.42, +0.18, +0.25) — upper left, in front half. Cube 2 at (+0.30, -0.28, +0.10) — right of and below cube 1. Cube 3 at (-0.05, -1.05, +0.15) — bottom center, sitting in the darker pool. Each cube carries its numeral (1, 2, 3) as a small black billboard glyph on its front face. Labels in tall parentheses, black serif-italic math: (Δm/ΔV)₁ anchored outside the vessel at upper right (~x +2.2, y +0.9), (Δm/ΔV)₂ at middle right (~x +2.3, y -0.25), (Δm/ΔV)₃ at left (~x -2.5, y -0.55). Thin black curved (quadratic) arrows with solid arrowheads run from each label to its cube: label 1 sweeps left-and-down into cube 1's right face, label 2 runs left into cube 2's right face, label 3 curves right-and-down into cube 3's left face. Density model: Uniform → ρ = 1000 kg/m³ at every cube. Heterogeneous → ρ(y) = 1000 + 55·(0.75 − y) kg/m³, giving ρ₁ ≈ 1031, ρ₂ ≈ 1057, ρ₃ ≈ 1099. Readout: ΔV = edge³ (report in cm³ with 1 world unit = 10 cm), Δm = ρ·ΔV, ratio shown to 0 decimals in kg/m³.
interactionPlan.notes: Render glass and liquid as MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission/opacity and depthWrite false, drawing the liquid before the outer wall so the wall's transparency sorts correctly. Dashed cube edges via LineSegments on EdgesGeometry with LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances); selected cube switches to a thicker, brighter dashed stroke plus a translucent amber fill. Labels, numerals and the Δm/ΔV readout as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so the math typography stays crisp and stays legible while orbiting; curved arrows as TubeGeometry along a QuadraticBezierCurve3 with a ConeGeometry head, kept in the camera-facing plane. Slider rescales the selected cube about its center only (scale, not translate) so it stays anchored at its sample point. Soft hemisphere + single key light, white background, no visible ground plane.

authoredContext:
The density of a substance is not necessarily constant throughout the volume of a substance. If the density is constant throughout a substance, the substance is said to be a homogeneous substance. A solid iron bar is an example of a homogeneous substance. The density is constant throughout, and the density of any sample of the substance is the same as its average density. If the density of a substance were not constant, the substance is said to be a heterogeneous substance. A chunk of Swiss cheese is an example of a heterogeneous material containing both the solid cheese and gas-filled voids. The density at a specific location within a heterogeneous material is called local density, and is given as a function of location, ρ=ρ(x,y,z) (the figure).

Density may vary throughout a heterogeneous mixture. Local density at a point is obtained from dividing mass by volume in a small volume around a given point.

Figure is a drawing of a container filled with a liquid. Small cubes are drawn in different regions of the container to indicate local density points.

Local density can be obtained by a limiting process, based on the average density in a small volume around the point in question, taking the limit where the size of the volume approaches zero,

discrepancies: The rolled rim/lip renders as a dark grey metallic torus rather than the pale, near-white translucent glass lip of the source, making the top of the vessel read as a metal ring.
Overall liquid/glass tint is greyer and more desaturated than the source's clearly light-blue liquid with a distinctly bluer bottom pool; the surface ellipse contrast is weaker.
The numerals 1/2/3 inside the dashed cubes are very small (13px) compared with the source, where they are prominent and clearly centered in each dashed box.

Cube-2 placement is less far right/low than in the source, so the staggered diagonal 1→2→3 arrangement is less pronounced; the arrow to cube 1 also crosses the free-surface ellipse rather than approaching cleanly from the right.
Selected cube is highlighted in orange/amber fill, an accent not present in the all-black-dashed source (acceptable as interaction feedback but changes the look at default state).
evaluation.notes: A recognizable, genuinely 3D reconstruction of the beaker with three dashed sample cubes and (Δm/ΔV)ₙ callouts, backed by well-designed interactions (cube selection, shrinking ΔV, uniform/heterogeneous model, guided demo); main weaknesses are colour fidelity (grey metallic rim, desaturated liquid) and undersized cube numerals.

Increase the cube numeral label font size (≈18-20px, bold) so 1/2/3 are as prominent as in the source, and keep (Δm/ΔV)ₙ as the primary hierarchy.

Nudge cube 2 further right and down and cube 3 slightly left so the 1→2→3 stagger matches the source, and re-route the cube-1 arrow so it approaches from the right without crossing the free-surface ellipse.
Soften the selected-cube amber fill (or make it an outline-only highlight) so the default state matches the source's plain black dashed boxes.

interactions.teaches: Density is evaluated at a chosen point: clicking cube 1, 2 or 3 highlights that dashed volume and shows its own Δm/ΔV, so the three are separate local numbers rather than one value for the whole vessel.

interactions.label: Sample cube edge (relative)
interactions.teaches: Shrinking the sampling cube makes Δm and ΔV both shrink, but their ratio settles on a fixed value — local density is the limit of Δm/ΔV as the surrounding volume becomes small.

interactions.label: Fluid model
interactions.teaches: In a uniform liquid all three ratios are equal (one bulk density); in a heterogeneous liquid the deeper cubes read larger ratios, so density becomes a function of position.
The three sample cubes sit at different depths and different distances into the vessel, not on a flat plane — rotating reveals their true 3D placement inside the liquid column.

demo_steps.title: One bulk density
demo_steps.narration: In a uniform liquid, each dashed cube returns the same Δm/ΔV. One number describes the whole vessel.

demo_steps.title: Sample cube 3 near the bottom
demo_steps.narration: Switch the fluid to heterogeneous: the deepest cube now measures a larger mass in the same volume, so (Δm/ΔV)₃ exceeds the others.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the sampling volume
demo_steps.narration: Drag the cube edge down. Δm and ΔV both collapse toward zero, yet their ratio stabilises — this limiting value is the local density at that point.

demo_steps.title: Compare all three points
demo_steps.narration: Back at full size, the three subscripted ratios are distinct numbers tied to three positions: density is defined point by point, not for the container as a whole.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Cylinder: radius 1.2, wall height 3.0, centered on origin with base at y = -1.5 and rim at y = +1.5. Rim lip: torus of tube radius 0.10 at y = +1.5, radius 1.22, pale opaque blue-white #e8f2f5; inner opening ellipse visible through it. Liquid: solid cylinder radius 1.15 from y = -1.48 up to a free surface at y = +0.75 (about one quarter of the height below the rim). Free-surface disc slightly darker #b6cbe6 with a thin darker rim band; bottom pooled region a darker ellipse #9dbcdc across y = -1.45. Glass wall transparent #dff0f2 at ~0.15 opacity with a faint lighter vertical highlight on the left; liquid body #c5d8ee at ~0.55 opacity. Sample cubes: wireframe boxes with black dashed edges (#1a1a1a), default edge length 0.42 (slider scales 0.1–1.0 of a 0.85 max edge). Cube 1 at (-0.42, +0.18, +0.25) — upper left, in front half. Cube 2 at (+0.30, -0.28, +0.10) — right of and below cube 1. Cube 3 at (-0.05, -1.05, +0.15) — bottom center, sitting in the darker pool. Each cube carries its numeral (1, 2, 3) as a small black billboard glyph on its front face. Labels in tall parentheses, black serif-italic math: (Δm/ΔV)₁ anchored outside the vessel at upper right (~x +2.2, y +0.9), (Δm/ΔV)₂ at middle right (~x +2.3, y -0.25), (Δm/ΔV)₃ at left (~x -2.5, y -0.55). Thin black curved (quadratic) arrows with solid arrowheads run from each label to its cube: label 1 sweeps left-and-down into cube 1's right face, label 2 runs left into cube 2's right face, label 3 curves right-and-down into cube 3's left face. Density model: Uniform → ρ = 1000 kg/m³ at every cube. Heterogeneous → ρ(y) = 1000 + 55·(0.75 − y) kg/m³, giving ρ₁ ≈ 1031, ρ₂ ≈ 1057, ρ₃ ≈ 1099. Readout: ΔV = edge³ (report in cm³ with 1 world unit = 10 cm), Δm = ρ·ΔV, ratio shown to 0 decimals in kg/m³.
interactionPlan.notes: Render glass and liquid as MeshPhysicalMaterial with transmission/opacity and depthWrite false, drawing the liquid before the outer wall so the wall's transparency sorts correctly. Dashed cube edges via LineSegments on EdgesGeometry with LineDashedMaterial (call computeLineDistances); selected cube switches to a thicker, brighter dashed stroke plus a translucent amber fill. Labels, numerals and the Δm/ΔV readout as CSS2DObject/HTML overlays so the math typography stays crisp and stays legible while orbiting; curved arrows as TubeGeometry along a QuadraticBezierCurve3 with a ConeGeometry head, kept in the camera-facing plane. Slider rescales the selected cube about its center only (scale, not translate) so it stays anchored at its sample point. Soft hemisphere + single key light, white background, no visible ground plane.

Liquid fill level and cube spacing differ slightly: in the source cube 2 is clearly lower-right and closer to the front wall; here cubes 1 and 2 are nearer the centre so the diagonal descent of the three sample points is less pronounced.
A 'Heterogeneous' fluid model (density varying with depth) is added; the source figure depicts only a single homogeneous liquid, so this is an extension beyond the original content.
